lessons.title: Welcome to digital safety
lessons.subtitle: Small habits, safer days
lessons.body:
Your phone helps you learn, work and connect. Keep it safe with a screen lock, current software and careful choices about what you share.

This course builds five useful habits. Read each short lesson, play its quiz, and finish with your own digital safety checklist.

questions.prompt: What should you set on your phone?
questions.explanation: A screen lock helps prevent other people from opening your phone.

questions.prompt: What helps fix known software problems?
questions.explanation: Updates can fix security problems. Install them from official sources.

questions.prompt: Before sharing personal information, you should…
questions.explanation: Share only what is needed with people or services you trust.

lessons.title: Staying safe online
lessons.subtitle: Build a stronger password
lessons.body:
Use a long, unique password for each account. A password manager can help you generate and store passwords. Turn on multi-factor authentication when available.

Never share your password or a one-time sign-in code. A support agent should not need them.

questions.prompt: Which choice best protects an account?
questions.explanation: A unique password limits the damage if another account is compromised.

questions.prompt: A caller asks for your sign-in code. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Sign-in codes can let someone access your account. Keep them private.

questions.prompt: What adds another layer of account protection?
options: Using your name as a password
questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication adds another check during sign-in.

lessons.title: Finding reliable information
lessons.subtitle: Check before you trust
lessons.body:
Anyone can publish online. Check who wrote a claim, when it was published, and what evidence supports it. Compare important claims with another credible source.

A professional-looking page or many likes do not prove a claim is true. When you are unsure, pause before sharing.

questions.prompt: What is useful when checking a claim?
questions.explanation: An identifiable author and supporting evidence help you assess a claim.

questions.prompt: A post makes a surprising claim. First…
questions.explanation: Comparing credible sources helps you spot unsupported claims.

questions.prompt: Does a polished website guarantee accurate information?
questions.explanation: Appearance and popularity are not evidence of accuracy.

lessons.title: Protecting personal information
lessons.subtitle: Share with intention
lessons.body:
Personal information includes your address, phone number and account details. Share only what a service really needs. Review app permissions and privacy settings.

Unexpected messages may try to make you act quickly. Avoid suspicious links. Open the official app or website yourself to check a request.

questions.prompt: A torch app requests your contacts. You should…
questions.explanation: Permissions should match what an app needs to do its job.

questions.prompt: An unexpected message says your account will close. You should…
questions.explanation: Use the official app or website to check unexpected account requests.

questions.prompt: What is safest to share publicly?
questions.explanation: General learning tips do not expose sensitive account or address details.

lessons.title: Your digital safety toolkit
lessons.subtitle: Turn learning into habits
lessons.body:
Bring your new skills together: use a screen lock, unique passwords, multi-factor authentication and careful sharing. Keep a backup of important files.

If you suspect an account problem, use official recovery tools and contact the service through a verified channel. Finish the course by creating your own safety checklist.

questions.explanation: A backup gives you another copy if a device or file is lost.

questions.prompt: Where should you start account recovery?
questions.explanation: Official recovery tools are the right starting point for account problems.

questions.prompt: What helps turn this course into a useful skill?
questions.explanation: A checklist helps you apply the habits you learned.
